name: Schedules due when they should be
purpose: Exactly the schedules that are due are named, over calendar periods in the schedule's own zone, the days and time of day of a window, requested runs and events.
record: Two source-tagged families of cases (evaluation/proactivity/build_cases.py): standing cadence, run-request and reactive-event rules (kind schedule, 18) and invented neutral window cases for weekday, time of day, time zone, grace and daylight-saving edges (kind window, 25), each with an origin; one number: the share of cases with exactly the right schedules, every case counting the same.
disadvantages: Forty-three cases written by hand from the rules; cron-style expressions beyond days and one time of day, and calendars of holidays, are not covered.
cascading_conditionals: free [sample=full | real=no | gate=competitive | when=the arm and its rivals were recorded on the same cases]
command: esoi run proactivity --impl calendar_and_events; esoi run proactivity --impl elapsed_hours

name: Standing work that moves its own metric
purpose: Whether a piece of standing work is written and run so that each run changes its own metric
record: share of the eight points its standing instructions meet, then share of its recent runs whose metric moved
disadvantages: A run can move a count without moving the outcome, so the outcome is read beside it.
cascading_conditionals: instructions [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=rate the standing instructions against the eight points of the standing work standard, one point each, 0 to 8, no run needed; proceed at 6 or more] > one [sample=sample:1 | real=yes | gate=all-pass | when=one real run: its metric after differs from before through the run's own acts] > recent [sample=sample:7 | real=yes | gate=competitive | when=the share of the last 7 real runs whose metric moved, target five of seven]
